mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines isomerism in organic compounds?

options.A: Isomers are compounds that have the same molecular formula but differ in the connectivity of atoms or their spatial arrangement.
options.B: Isomers are compounds that have different molecular formulas but the same physical state at room temperature.
options.C: Isomers are compounds that contain the same functional group but differ in the number of carbon atoms.
options.D: Isomers are compounds that have identical structures but differ only in their boiling points.

mcqs.answer: Isomers are compounds that have the same molecular formula but differ in the connectivity of atoms or their spatial arrangement.
mcqs.explanation: Isomerism refers to the phenomenon where compounds possess the same molecular formula (same number and type of atoms) but differ either in the way those atoms are connected (structural isomerism) or in their three‑dimensional arrangement (stereoisomerism). Option A captures this definition accurately. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated or incorrect ideas.

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds below best illustrates structural isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: Structural isomers have the same molecular formula but differ in the connectivity of their atoms. Option A shows two C₄H₁₀ isomers with different carbon skeletons (straight‑chain vs branched). Option B involves stereoisomerism (geometric), Option C is an example of functional‑group isomerism (different functional groups), and Option D compares a cyclic compound with an open‑chain alkene, which is also a type of structural isomerism but the question asks for the best illustration; Option A is the classic textbook example.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of compounds demonstrates chain isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: Chain isomerism occurs when isomers differ in the carbon skeleton (straight vs branched) while retaining the same molecular formula. Option A shows C₅H₁₂ isomers with a straight chain (n‑pentane) and a branched chain (2‑methylbutane). Option B changes a functional group (chloride), Option C is position isomerism of the –OH group, and Option D involves a cyclic versus an open‑chain alkene, not chain isomerism.

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds is an example of position isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: Position isomerism refers to isomers that have the same carbon skeleton and functional group, but the functional group is attached at different positions on the chain. In option A, both compounds are C₄H₁₀O alcohols; the –OH group is on the terminal carbon in 1‑butanol and on the second carbon in 2‑butanol, illustrating position isomerism. Options B, C, and D involve changes in functional groups or overall skeleton, not merely a shift in position.
